# Best portable power station for camping

For most campers, the best choice is a small 250-500Wh unit. It's light enough to pack, and it covers phones, lights, a camera, and a CPAP. Go bigger only if you want to run a fridge or appliances.

## My picks

**Best overall for most trips: Jackery Explorer 300 Plus (~$249)**
- 288Wh LiFePO4, 300W output, about 8.3 lb.
- PowerStationGearLab's top pick. It says it runs phones, lights, and a CPAP for multiple nights.
- [Buy link via PowerStationGearLab's guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) (its "Check price on Amazon" button)

**Alternatives in the same size class** (same guide):
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus (~$269-299):** 600W inverter, double the Jackery's.
- **Anker SOLIX C300 (~$199):** a good value for longer trips.
- **Bluetti EB3A (~$179):** the budget pick, with a 600W inverter.

**Best for a mid-size setup: Bluetti AC180 ($499)**
- 1,152Wh, 1,800W output, about 35 lb (16 kg), and a 5-year warranty.
- It can run kitchen appliances and charge power tools, and it accepts up to 500W of solar.
- A discount code (AFF5OFF) was reported to take $24.95 off, bringing it to $474.05. That was tested on 2026-10-21, and the store's checkout has the final word.
- [Buy at BLUETTI's official US store](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. [Source page](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180).
- Caveat: the $499 price is the station alone. The $599 option includes a 100W solar panel.

**Best value in the 1kWh class: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (under ~$530)**
- OutdoorGearLab's best value for most people.
- It covers off-grid camping, blackouts, and general portable power.
- [See OutdoorGearLab's review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

**Best for van life or a 12V fridge: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (~$799)**
- 1,070Wh, 1,500W, about 23.8 lb.
- PowerStationGearLab and TechRadar both pick it for camping.
- [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) · [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)

**Best for multi-day off-grid trips: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (under ~$900)**
- OutdoorGearLab's pick for extended camping. It weighs 39 lb, and solar recharging is easy to add.
- [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

WIRED picked the Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra ($1,199, listed at $1,079) as its best for camping. [WIRED's guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## Quick sizing tips
- Rough usage: about 10Wh per phone charge, 30-60Wh per night for a CPAP, and about 5Wh per lantern night.
- Turn off the CPAP humidifier. It can triple the machine's draw.
- Add up the watts of what you'll run and multiply by hours. A 150W fridge for 10 hours is about 1,500Wh.
- These units exceed the 100Wh airline limit, so they're for car camping, not flights.

## Caveats
- Only the Bluetti has a direct retailer link in my search results. For the others, use the buy buttons on the linked review pages, since I couldn't confirm direct product URLs.
- Prices vary between sources and change often, so confirm the current price at checkout.
- Several of these guides use affiliate links, but they agree on the main picks.

If you tell me your trip length and what you need to power, I can narrow this to one pick.
